text:
Maria R: hitting a weird correctness issue in the cache after a long-context run. memory grows and some later requests return tokens that clearly belong to previous sessions.
Aj Patel: yikes. repro on prod or staging? any logs?
Maria R: staging. repro by streaming 8k+ context then a short request. sometimes the short request gets tokens from the earlier long one. not every time, maybe 1/20.
Simon K: do you have the request ids and the low-level tags? that smells like a tag/offset mixup on page reuse.
Maria R: pasted a minimal trace: 
```
[2026-03-10T17:02:11Z] tag=0x7f3a5b req=stg-387 id=0x112 offset=4096 len=512
[2026-03-10T17:02:11Z] serve: hit page=27 frame=3 owner=req-123
[2026-03-10T17:02:15Z] tag=0x8c1b9f req=stg-388 id=0x113 offset=0 len=32
[2026-03-10T17:02:15Z] serve: hit page=27 frame=3 owner=req-123 <-- wrong owner
```
Maria R: the second short request should have unique frames but it shows owner=req-123.
InfraBot: incident alert: kv-cache:owner-clash threshold exceeded for staging cluster-2 (count=7)
Leo T: can you dump the eviction queue and page metadata around the time? maybe we forgot to clear owner tag on eviction.
Maria R: eviction log shows page 27 was evicted then reallocated without re-tagging in some runs. attaching snippet: 
```
EVICT page=27 tomb=0x0 -> allocated frame=3 tag=0x8c1b9f owner=req-388
ALLOC frame=3 map.entry.tag still=0x7f3a5b owner=req-123
```
Aj Patel: that looks like an incomplete init after alloc. which code path allocates + initializes? continuous-batching fastpath might do a shallow reset to avoid perf hit.
Simon K: yes, recent PR changed the fastpath to skip a memset for speed when page size unchanged — possible regression. PR: runtime:opt-fast-reuse #4521.
Elaine S: profiling notes: after PR we saw 12% lower p99 for batched generation but memory tagging regressions show up in long runs. pprof heap growth aligns with pages not being zeroed.
Leo T: good find. Maria, can you try flipping the fastpath gate at runtime and repro? I can push a toggle.
Maria R: tried toggle -> when fastpath disabled, no contamination after 500 runs. with fastpath enabled, contamination resumes ~1/18.
Aj Patel: for immediate mitigation we should ensure owner/tag are cleared on alloc path even if we skip memset. quick patch: set frame.tag=0 and frame.owner=NONE before marking available.
Simon K: agree. add an assert in debug builds to catch reuse without init. also add a repro unit that fuzzes alloc/free under long-context churn.
Maria R: I'll open a PR with failing test and simple fix. also adding a small reproducer in e2e that runs 10k short requests interleaved with a long ones.
Elaine S: upstream note: kernel selection/batching heuristics contributed to frequency — larger batches made alloc cadence different so bug surface varies with batch size. logging that in the PR.
Aj Patel: note for rollout: this is correctness -> hotfix roll to staging and prod with immediate rollback plan. performance delta expected ~0.5% p99.
InfraBot: deploy pipeline: build passed, staging deploy queued for canary.
Maria R: PR: https://git.company/repo/pull/5847 will contain test, fix, and assert. tagging @Aj Patel for rollout.
Leo T: once merged let's run long-run soak overnight on staging cluster-2. if green, schedule prod canary at 2am window.
Maria R: thanks. saved traces and heap dumps in /mnt/artifacts/kv-align-2141592600 for postmortem.
Simon K: extra: add metric for "uninitialized-reuse" to catch any future fastpath changes.
Elaine S: noted. also let's add a note in release notes under "runtime: fixed cache reuse/tagging bug causing cross-request contamination"
Maria R: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
